A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Adapt-∞ research, with readable methods, equations, results, figures, and appendices. Retained content can be matched despite resizing and relocation, including the multilingual-recovery analysis moved into v2's appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original instruction-tuning experiments, baseline comparisons, component ablations, skill-recovery analyses, and efficiency-variant results in Tables 2–3 and 5 and Figures 3–6.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds runtime measurements, scoring-function results, visual-chat examples, and language-only instruction-tuning results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: Gradient-based pseudo-task clustering, entropy-based scorer selection, CCS sampling, image-grounding scoring, and optional permanent semantic pruning remain unchanged. The language-only application does not specify a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix C adds language-only training on Natural Instructions, Alpaca-CoT, xP3, UltraChat, and FireFly. Evaluation includes GSM, BBH, TydiQA, CodexEval, and AlpacaEval alongside the previously used MMLU, substantially extending task and data coverage. A multi-turn visual-chat scenario is also added; the original multimodal coverage remains.

E2.justification: LESS (Xia et al., 2024), previously only cited, becomes an evaluated runtime comparator in v2's Table 6. The original accuracy-comparison methods in Table 2 are unchanged. The new language-only and chat experiments use existing comparator types.

E3.justification: The original LLaVA protocol and metrics remain unchanged. Added evaluations use LLaMA3-8B with 25k training samples per timestep, a single-example chat comparison at t=0 and t=5, and separate timing of scoring, clustering, and training. Table 7 does not specify its ablation budget, preventing a reliable matched-setting comparison with earlier ablations.

E4.justification: Appendix C adds a computational-cost breakdown, an ablation removing image grounding from the scorer pool, and a visual-chat retention case study. These substantially expand analysis of cost, component dependence, and behavior. The multilingual-recovery experiment is retained as Figure 9, relocated from v1's Section 6 and Figure 6.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added experiments introduce no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Tables 2, 3, and 5 retain their numerical results. v2 adds runtime measurements, the no-image-grounding ablation row, chat outputs, and language-only results. Table 8 reports LITE-Adapt-∞ accuracy of 43.1 and forgetting of 2.3%, versus random selection's 41.8 and 5.6%. These are additional results, not improvements to the unchanged original multimodal scores.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(4), the constrained training objective, image-grounding definition, entropy-selection rule, and evaluation-metric definitions are unchanged. Neither version adds theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: the LiIT setting, adaptive multi-way selection, permanent pruning, reduced forgetting, and forward transfer. Replacing 'Lifelong' with 'Continual' in the title does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds interpretations linking chat retention to preserving a conversational pseudo-task, scorer flexibility to the new ablation, and applicability to language-only learning. It also discusses measured gradient-extraction overhead and acknowledges the single-example qualitative chat evaluation. The earlier multilingual-recovery interpretation is retained.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports timing on eight A100 GPUs, component-level computation times, and the language-only experiment's model, training order, sample budget, and FireFly access link. The existing 8192-dimensional random projection and code-access information remain unchanged; no corresponding alteration of the original implementation is established.

R1.justification: Six references are added for the language-only model, datasets, and evaluation setup, including Dubey et al., Mishra et al., and Wang et al. The existing related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title terminology and publication header, tightens introductory paragraphs, explicitly enumerates the setting's challenges, and corrects several typos. It adds Appendix C and moves the multilingual-recovery discussion there, while preserving most existing prose and the main section sequence.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 6–8 and three extensive visual-chat displays in Figures 6–8. It also revises diagram styling and labels, resizes several main-text figures and tables, relocates Table 3, and moves the original recovery plot to appendix Figure 9. The display changes extend well beyond renumbering.

improvement.justification: Runtime measurements in Table 6 and language-only validation in Table 8 improve transparency and broaden evidence beyond v1. The gain is limited by Table 7's unspecified budgets and ambiguous relationship to the retained image-grounding ablation. The chat-retention interpretation also exceeds what one example containing clear output errors establishes. Overall, the new quantitative evidence provides a useful but qualified improvement.
